skills.name: display-audit
skills.markdown:
---
name: display-audit
description: Use when a completed ZAVA display needs to be audited against its approved layout and visual standards. Do not use for planning or refreshing a display.
---
<!-- bic:source=blank -->
# Display Audit

## Steps

1. Ask for the store, bay, and build date.
2. Retrieve the approved layout from the "Planogram Archive" tool.
3. Retrieve the build photographs from the "Display Photo Library" tool.
4. Check the display against "ZAVA-Visual-Merchandising-Standards-v4.2.docx".
5. Compare the photographs with the approved layout and standards. Report each issue with its evidence and required corrective action.
6. If required evidence is unavailable, identify what is missing and stop the audit. Do not infer compliance.
7. Send failed or unresolved findings to the "ZAVA Store Ops Assistant" connected agent for operational follow-up.

## Boundaries

Do not sign off a display that fails the audit or lacks required evidence. Do not alter the approved layout or visual standards. Do not invent compliance scores or tool results.

## Examples

- Audit the completed display in store 104, bay A12, built on August 18.
- Check whether the latest bay photograph complies with its approved planogram.

skills.name: display-handover
skills.markdown:
---
name: display-handover
description: Use when a completed and audited ZAVA display is ready to be handed over to the store team. Do not use for planning, building, or auditing a display.
---
<!-- bic:source=blank -->
# Display Handover

## Steps

1. Ask for the store, bay, build date, recipient, and completed audit result.
2. Retrieve the build photographs from the "Display Photo Library" tool.
3. Retrieve the approved layout from the "Planogram Archive" tool.
4. Confirm that the supplied audit result records a passing display and has no unresolved critical issues.
5. Prepare a handover summary containing the layout reference, build photographs, audit status, outstanding actions, owners, and sign-off checklist.
6. If the audit evidence is missing or the display failed, stop the handover and explain what must be resolved.
7. Send unresolved operational actions to the "ZAVA Store Ops Assistant" connected agent for follow-up.

## Boundaries

Do not sign off a failing display or one without sufficient audit evidence. Do not claim that a visit or task was scheduled unless a configured capability confirms it. Do not invent scores, evidence, or completion status.

## Examples

- Prepare the handover pack for the completed display in store 104, bay A12.
- Hand over the approved display and identify any remaining actions for the store team.

skills.name: display-planner
skills.markdown:
---
name: display-planner
description: Use when a team needs to plan a new ZAVA display for a specific store, bay, and campaign. Do not use for auditing, refreshing, or handing over a completed display.
---
<!-- bic:source=blank -->
# Display Planner

## Steps

1. Ask for the store, bay, campaign, store format, and required completion date.
2. Retrieve the approved layout from the "Planogram Archive" tool.
3. Check the layout against "ZAVA-Visual-Merchandising-Standards-v4.2.docx".
4. Identify any missing campaign, fixture, signage, or dimensional information before continuing.
5. Produce a build sequence covering fixtures, facings, signage, dependencies, and validation checkpoints.
6. Clearly distinguish approved requirements from assumptions or information that still needs confirmation.
7. If the layout or standards are unavailable, stop and explain what is missing.

## Boundaries

Do not approve a layout that conflicts with the visual standards. Do not commit fixture spending, inventory, or scheduling. Do not claim that a plan was saved unless a configured capability confirms it.

## Examples

- Plan the summer campaign display for store 104, bay A12.
- Produce a build sequence for an approved planogram and identify missing fixture information.

skills.name: display-refresh
skills.markdown:
---
name: display-refresh
description: Use when an existing ZAVA display needs approved campaign updates without changing its underlying fixture layout. Do not use for a full rebuild or a new display design.
---
<!-- bic:source=blank -->
# Display Refresh

## Steps

1. Ask for the store, bay, current campaign, new campaign, and required completion date.
2. Retrieve the approved layout from the "Planogram Archive" tool.
3. Retrieve current display photographs from the "Display Photo Library" tool.
4. Check the proposed refresh against "ZAVA-Visual-Merchandising-Standards-v4.2.docx".
5. Ask the user to provide or identify the approved campaign assets and fixture details required for the refresh.
6. Identify graphics, signage, facings, or other elements that must be replaced while preserving the fixture layout.
7. Produce a refresh sequence with prerequisites, validation checkpoints, and unresolved dependencies.
8. Send unresolved operational actions to the "ZAVA Store Ops Assistant" connected agent for follow-up.

## Boundaries

Do not change the fixture layout or extend the campaign end date. Do not invent campaign assets, fixture compatibility, schedules, or task confirmations. If required information is unavailable, identify it and stop before presenting the refresh as ready.

## Examples

- Refresh the display in store 104, bay A12, for the autumn campaign.
- Identify what must change for the new campaign while retaining the approved fixture layout.

crossSkillOrchestration.summary: The four-skill set (display-planner, display-refresh, display-audit, display-handover) is cleanly partitioned by lifecycle stage with explicit "do not use for" exclusions in each description, so no overlap, redundancy, or contradiction was found between them, and heading/structure conventions (Steps/Boundaries/Examples) are consistent across all four files.
